title: Shipped defaults: open to the world, admin on, no password
root_cause: The program's out-of-the-box configuration binds to every network interface, turns on an administrative feature, and accepts an empty password -- and nothing refuses to start in that state. Most deployments run with defaults untouched, so the default IS the real-world security posture for a large share of installs.
defenses: Make the safe choice the default: bind to localhost, disable admin/debug features, require explicit opt-in.
Validate configuration at startup and refuse to run (fail closed) in a clearly unsafe combination.
Document every default clearly, and treat changing an insecure default as a breaking-but-necessary change.
Scan shipped configuration files and container images for known-bad defaults as part of release.
